'''Cuba''' (''Tsucuba''), anglicized as '''Shuba''' and also known as '''Urcibar''' in neighboring [[Lopa language|Lopa]], is a minor [[Kainji language]] of [[Nigeria]], spoken by a thousand people in [[Kebbi State]].

The name Rerang (Oleran) subsumes both Cuba and the closely related [[Lopa language]] that surrounds it.<ref name="Blench">{{Cite web|last=Blench|first=Roger|url=http://www.rogerblench.info/Language/Niger-Congo/BC/Kainji/General/Kainji%20language%20overview.pdf|title=The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria|publisher=Kay Williamson Educational Foundation|year=2012|location=Cambridge}}</ref><ref name="McGillKainji">McGill, Stuart. 2012. The Kainji languages. Ms, School of Oriental and African Studies, London, 30 August 2012.</ref>

Blench concludes that Cuba is more closely related to Shen ([[Laru language|Laru]]) than it is to Rop (Lopa).<ref name="Blench" />

==Location==
Cuba is spoken in the large villages of {{IPA|ò̃tʃébá}} (Cifamini), {{IPA|tʷò̃tʃíɡí}} (Gungun Tagwaye) and {{IPA|ò̃sán}} (Kwanga); and the minor villages of {{IPA|àjũ ́̃m}} (Yumu), {{IPA|àːʔʲɔ́}} (Bakari) and {{IPA|ámbú}} (Ambu shiri).
